needed some extra work. better fr #10 screw bracket than #8 - the cams for the upper and lower part seem to be a different material....the lower feels denser. the fit was fine in my 19 year old side by side refrig. the problem was that the better screws that secure the lower half to the bracket were too big to fit in my bracket, and the ones supplied that were my size did not have this little offset section to keep the cam from sliding back and forth when the refrig was opened all the way. in other words, the diameter of the hole for the screw in the cam was too large for the screw(without the offset) for my bracket. in the end, I had to enlarge this hole to 3/8 and put a washer in there to act as a spacer and a bigger washer on top of that. after this, worked perfectly. maybe it is the age of this refrigerator..in other words, the #10 screws with the offset, if this fits the bracket, works far better than the #8 ones. according to the instructions, it could be either. I guess the #10, which works the best, looks like a shoulder bolt with a very narrow shoulder. The #8 has no shoulder, thus, allowing for the slippage.

DIY Euphoria - Dryer was making a super loud knocking sound. Found out on you tube that the wheels needed to be replaced.

Dryer appliance repair technician quoted some astronomical price to replace the wheels in our dryer.

Watched the videos on you tube and proceed on our own with these wheels. FYI these wheels do not come with the piece/shaft that goes thru the center. So not sure why it is referred to as an "assembly."

However, for the rear wheels which is 2 of the four it is actually easier if one does not try to install new shafts and simply replaces the wheel on the existing shaft.

However, a word to the wise. This is not rocket science but it is "screw" science. There were a boat load of screws. So we used zip loc bags to collect each set of screws and labeled each bag to remind us what screws went where.

In hindsight if we ever have to do it again we would also add a # to each bag. So the first set of screws would go in a zip loc bag labeled #1 with a written description plus take a corresponding picture with a smartphone in case by the time we got to bag #17 the description say for bag #3 was meaningless because of the obvious learning curve. Took 2 people, the newbie diy home tech and the screw tech assistant the better part of 2 days to complete the repair.

But when we were done, the dryer worked beautifully like new, very quite.

We only had 1 screw leftover when we were done. But hey! Saved a hefty cache of cash :-) And garnered some serious diy euphoria!

There are a few important things to keep in mind

#1. This ice maker does NOT keep the ice which is made frozen. It drops into the bin. .. then melts and is recycled if you do not use it. If you want to keep it frozen. . . You'll need to place it into your own freezer.

#2. Though the listing shows that this ice maker can make 26# of ice in 24-hours. . . That's only if you have someone standing there to empty the bin each time it is full. . . day-and-night. So that part is really no realistic.

#3. "Self-Cleaning" is a misnomer. When you turn-on the "self-cleaning" cycle. .. All that happens is that the water is cycled through again and again until you stop it. So there's really not a lot of cleaning going on unless you add something to the water. There's no information about what to add. You can do your own research. . but. . . I actually use the same cleaner I use with my espresso maker for descaling.

This ice maker is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. There are lots of these same machines being sold by Chinese companies right now on Amazon, so make sure you look around for the best price before purchasing.

Stops a Speed Queen washer from walking around the laundry room - We have a Speed Queen Commercial washing machine ( LFNE5BSP113TW01) in our home. This thing is a 270 pound beast, and it really cleans so much better than the newer Samsung it replaced. The issue that I had with it is that it is installed on a tile floor that is a little slippery. This washer uses more water than most front loaders (probably the reason it actually gets clothes clean), and when it enters the rinse or spin cycles, it will naturally oscillate a little while it balances the load. When the washer would oscillate, it would slowly walk around to a spot where it was no longer in balance on the floor (it's a tile floor, and not perfectly level in all spots). When it hit that place, it would start vibrating and dancing around like crazy. If you gave it a gentle push back to it's original position, the vibration would cease immediately. I needed some pads to keep this machine from moving on the floor, and absorb some of the vibration, and these have done the job perfectly. The washer is so much quieter now, and I'm sure that is resulting in less wear on the machine. I was concerned whether or not these would be large enough inside diameter for this big washer, but they fit perfectly, and they work great!. Front load washers ought to be shipped with these things.
